translation.title: Analgesic and Anti-inflammatory Plaster
translation.efficacy: This medicine is used for shoulder pain due to stiff shoulders, low back pain, joint pain, muscle pain, tenosynovitis (pain and swelling of the hand, wrist and ankle), elbow pain (such as tennis elbow), bruises and sprains.
translation.usage: Apply the patch to the affected area once or twice a day.
translation.caution: Do not use this medicine in the following cases: people who are hypersensitive to this medicine or other felbinac preparations; people who have experienced asthma, urticaria or acute rhinitis with aspirin or other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs; women who are pregnant, may be pregnant, or are breastfeeding; children under 15 years of age; the area around the eyes and mucous membranes; eczema; inflamed areas; athlete’s foot; insect-bitten areas; suppurating areas; wounded areas. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before using this medicine in the following cases: people who have experienced allergic symptoms from medicines. Bathing with the patch on causes strong irritation, so remove it at least 30 minutes before bathing. Do not warm the area where the patch is applied with a heater, an electric blanket or the like. Do not use it for more than 2 consecutive weeks. People with delicate skin must not use it repeatedly on the same area. Follow the prescribed dosage and directions. If you are sweating or the affected area is wet, wipe it dry before use. If your symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. Stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist if occasional redness, rash, itching, swelling, stinging, inflammation, blisters or shock occur (urticaria, swelling or chest discomfort immediately after use, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing). Store at room temperature, protected from moisture and light. Keep out of reach of children. Keep unused patches in the pouch with the zipper closed.
